text:
Alex Newhook won a Stanley Cup with Colorado in 2022 and is now in his third season in Montreal. On the scoresheet he is doing fine: 5 goals and 10 points in 21 games, 4 of the goals in his last ten, and his shooting matches his chances (5 goals on 4.8 expected goals, the quality of his shots).

The underlying numbers are harsher. At five on five Montreal takes only 38.6% of the expected goals with him on the ice, 16.2 points worse than the team without him. The players he most resembles statistically share one trait: chances against pile up with them on. Evolving-Hockey had a similar story last season, with his team creating 0.15 fewer expected goals per 60 when he played (bottom 9% of forwards).

His minutes are already sliding. After four straight games of 17.8 minutes or more, he has played between 12.2 and 15.7 in each of his last six. Against Colorado on Nov. 14 he had a tip waved off as "too high," The Hockey News' Karine Hains posted. For a forward whose goals are keeping him afloat, the five-on-five results are the number to watch.
